name: Yoruba religion
title: The story of the Yoruba religion

text: The Yoruba live mainly in south-western Nigeria and in nearby Benin and Togo.
In one Yoruba story, Oduduwa finished making dry land on the waters, founded Ife and became its first king.
src: living mainly in south-western Nigeria and in neighbouring Benin and Togo
In one widely told myth / to make dry land on the primeval waters / his brother Oduduwa completed the task, founded Ife and became its first king

text: Yoruba tradition holds that Ile-Ife is the place where the world was created.
The city grew strong about 1,000 years ago, and its artists made lifelike heads of copper alloy.
src: Ile-Ife, which Yoruba tradition regards as the place where the world was created
The city flourished from around 1000 CE / its artists cast naturalistic heads in copper alloy

text: Believers worship Olodumare, the supreme god, through the orisha, divine powers who carry out his will.
Eshu is the messenger and trickster, who guards crossroads and doorways.
src: worships Olodumare, the supreme god / is approached through the orisha, the divine powers who carry out his will in the world
Eshu, the messenger and trickster, guardian of crossroads and doorways

text: Every August, thousands of worshippers come to the sacred grove of Oshun, the river goddess.
Priests called babalawo use Ifa, a way of seeking guidance, and may know thousands of its verses by heart.
src: Every August the Osun-Osogbo festival draws thousands of worshippers and visitors to the river goddess’s sacred grove
a system of divination practised by priests called babalawo / a master may know thousands of verses by heart

text: Enslaved Yoruba carried their faith across the Atlantic Ocean, many of them to Cuba and Brazil.
There it grew into new faiths: Santería in Cuba and Candomblé in Brazil.
src: Carried across the Atlantic by enslaved Yoruba / many of them to Cuba and to Bahia in Brazil
it gave rise to Santería in Cuba, Candomblé in Brazil

text: Today most Yoruba are Christians or Muslims, but festivals and Ifa are still part of their lives.
The orisha are now worshipped in Nigeria, Benin, Cuba, Brazil, the United States and beyond.
src: Today most Yoruba are Christians or Muslims, but traditional festivals, kingship rituals and the consultation of Ifa remain part of public and private life
its gods are worshipped today in Nigeria, Benin, Cuba, Brazil, Trinidad, the United States and beyond
